observations: Photo 0 shows a large solar panel leaning against a white cabinet or enclosure, with a black box and wires attached to the cabinet. The panel has a grid of dark photovoltaic cells with white diamond-shaped gaps between them.
Photo 1 is a close-up of a label on the back of the solar panel. The label clearly shows the brand 'CanadianSolar' and model 'CS3K-300M'.
The label lists technical specifications: Nominal Maximum Power (Pmax) 300W, Open Circuit Voltage (Voc) 39.7V, Short Circuit Current (Isc) 9.88A, and other data.
The label includes a QR code, safety warnings, and certification marks (CE, etc.).
The photos are watermarked with 'FRANK SOLAR ENTERPRISES' and timestamped 27/03/2025.
The seller's text mentions 'solar panel, inverter and batteries of different sizes' but only the solar panel is shown in the photos.

claims.claim: we have solar panel, inverter and batteries of different sizes
claims.evidence: Only the solar panel is shown in the photos. No inverter or batteries are visible.
Photo 0 shows a solar panel, and photo 1 confirms it with a label.
Only one panel is shown; no other sizes are visible in the photos.

risks.risk: The panel may be damaged or defective (e.g., cracked cells, internal faults) not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the front surface of the panel showing all cells, and a video of the panel being tested under sunlight or with a multimeter.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially non-functional or with reduced efficiency.

risks.risk: The panel may not be genuine or may be a counterfeit CanadianSolar product.
risks.proof: A video of the QR code being scanned, showing the official CanadianSolar website or product page, and a photo of the serial number being verified on the manufacturer's site.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially counterfeit, which would reduce value significantly.

risks.risk: The panel may have been previously installed or used, with hidden wear or degradation.
risks.proof: A photo of the back of the panel showing mounting holes, wiring, or signs of previous installation, and a video of the panel being tilted to check for cell cracks or discoloration.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as used, with potential efficiency loss.

proof_requests: Send a close-up photo of the front surface of the solar panel showing all cells without glare.
Send a video of the panel being tested under sunlight or with a multimeter to verify output.
Scan the QR code on the label and send a screenshot of the official CanadianSolar product page.
Send a photo of the serial number and verify it on the CanadianSolar website.
Send a photo of the back of the panel showing any mounting holes, wiring, or signs of previous use.
response.reason: The solar panel is clearly identified as a CanadianSolar CS3K-300M model from the label in photo 1. The photos show the item, and while there are hidden risks (damage, counterfeit, used condition), these are common for second-hand solar panels and can be priced at worst case. The seller's claim of having other items (inverter, batteries) is unverified but does not affect the price of the panel shown.
